subject: Scaling playbook: reserved hours & per-hour repricing for 16→32 GPU renewal
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Megan Li <megan@atlasdata.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 1 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Scaling playbook: reserved hours & per-hour repricing for 16→32 GPU renewal

Hi Megan —

Thanks again for the time last week. Per our conversation about AtlasData's renewal window, I put together a concise proposal for moving from your current 16-GPU reserved pool to a 32-GPU committed configuration for the 12-month renewal. High level:

- Staged ramp: month 1–3 keep 16 GPUs reserved + burst pool; month 4 onboard additional 16 GPUs to reach full 32 reserved.
- Blended per-hour reserved rate: we propose a two-tier rate that lowers incremental per-hour pricing for the second 16 GPUs (details in attached spreadsheet).
- Throughput guarantee: baseline throughput (tokens/sec) guarantee paired with p99 latency SLOs and a credit mechanism if we miss targets (see SLA appendix).

I've attached Reserved_PRICING_v3.xlsx (breakdown by zone and blended vs flat pricing) and SLA-throughput-appendix.pdf. Can we schedule a 30-min sync early next week to walk through the numbers and confirm procurement requirements? If you prefer, I can share an amendment draft after we align on committed hours/month.

Next steps:
1) Quick call — propose Mon Aug 3, 11am PT or Tue Aug 4, 9am PT
2) I'll loop Lauren for final pricing approval and Marissa for contract language once we agree on the structure

Thanks — looking forward to getting this in place in time for your usage spike in Q4.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: Reserved_PRICING_v3.xlsx (spreadsheet), SLA-throughput-appendix.pdf (PDF)

Thanks, Megan — calendar invite sent for Tue 9am PT. Quick answers ahead of the call so procurement has context: 

- Committed hours/month at full 32 GPUs: 720 reserved GPU-hours per GPU-class (we break out instance types in the spreadsheet); in practice, the amendment will list a monthly committed pool (e.g., 32 GPUs * 720 hours = 23,040 reserved GPU-hours).
- Credit structure: service credits up to 10% of the monthly reserved charge if throughput baseline (tokens/sec averaged over 24h windows) falls below the SLA target for more than two non-consecutive 24h windows in a month. We can convert to an hourly refund if procurement needs line-item reductions on the invoice.
- Ramp flexibility: yes — we can accelerate to a month-2 completion with a prorated invoice for the additional GPUs for the partial month (spreadsheet has pro-rata formulas).

I've highlighted the key rows in Reserved_PRICING_v3.xlsx: "Base 16-GPU rate", "Incremental 16-GPU discount", and the "Prorate calculator" tab. Lauren — can you confirm the blended rate approvals on your end? Marissa — please flag any term language we should lock before sending a draft amendment to AtlasData.

Ben
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Megan / Procurement team —

Thanks for the clear asks. Per our call and internal approvals:

- PO line items: we'll provide three PO-ready lines in the amendment: (1) Reserved GPU-hours – Base 16 GPUs @ $1.95/hr per GPU; (2) Incremental reserved GPU-hours – Additional 16 GPUs @ $1.30/hr per GPU; (3) Burst/Spot pool (optional) @ $0.65/hr when used. Totals will be calculated from the committed monthly GPU-hours (32 * 720 = 23,040 hours).
- Credit mechanism: will be issued as a credit memo after monthly close (fits your accounting preference). Credit calc: up to 10% of the monthly reserved invoice if SLA misses trigger (detailed in SLA-throughput-appendix.pdf).
- Scale-down notice: standard 60 days written notice; reductions will be prorated to the effective date but require a minimum 3-month commitment at the lower tier to avoid churn overhead (we've found that fixed operating capacity requires a short-term floor).
- Ramp: we can accelerate to month 2 with a pro-rata invoice for additional reserved hours for any partial month.

Next steps I will take now: Lauren will issue a final price confirmation and I will drop a draft amendment in DocuSign with the three PO line items and the 12-month term. Link to the DocuSign will be posted here for your procurement team to review.

DocuSign link (live once I upload): https://www.docusign.net/ATD-amendment-2026

If that aligns, I'll upload the amendment and flag Marissa to run a quick legal review before sending.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
